meta.title: KISSA MIDORI | 喫茶みどり — Matcha Café in Gion, Kyoto
meta.description: Kissa Midori is a warm, wa-modern matcha café in Gion, Kyoto. First-harvest Uji matcha served in a 120-year-old machiya townhouse. English-speaking staff — travelers welcome.

hero.titleJp:
A Sip of Green,
A Moment of Calm.
hero.titleEn: みどり、ひとくち。心、ほどける。
hero.sub:
First-harvest Uji matcha, served slowly on a townhouse veranda.
Whether it's your first bowl or your hundredth — you're always welcome.

about.label: About Us
about.title:
Green,
made with care.
about.lead: Kissa Midori is a small matcha café tucked into a quiet lane in Gion, Kyoto.
about.body1: "Matcha doesn't have to be difficult." That belief is where Kissa Midori began. We work directly with Uji tea farmers and serve first-harvest matcha — stone-ground that very morning — one bowl at a time.
about.body2: Set in a restored 120-year-old machiya townhouse, the room is filled with seasonal tea flowers and soft, dappled light. Drop in between sightseeing, let your shoulders drop, and stay as long as you like.

menu.label: Our Menu
menu.title: Seasonal Menu
menu.subtitle: Gentle flavors, all born from first-harvest Uji matcha.
menu.note: Menu changes with the seasons. Please let our staff know about any allergies. All prices include tax.

items.name: Usucha
items.desc: A bowl whisked by hand with a bamboo chasen. Savor the vivid green and mellow sweetness of first-harvest matcha.

items.name: Koicha
items.desc: Three times the usual tea leaves for a rich, concentrated bowl with deep umami and a long finish.

items.name: Matcha Latte
items.desc: A gentle harmony of Kyoto milk and matcha. Enjoy it warm, or over ice.

items.name: Matcha Parfait
items.desc: Layers of matcha ice cream, shiratama mochi, sweet red bean, and matcha jelly. As lovely to look at as it is to eat.

items.name: Warabi Mochi
items.desc: Made with 100% real bracken starch. A melt-in-the-mouth texture, dusted generously with stone-ground matcha and kinako.

items.name: Matcha Terrine
items.desc: A smooth, rich matcha terrine that melts on the tongue — the perfect balance of bittersweet in a single slice.

items.name: Matcha + Seasonal Wagashi
items.desc: The day's first-harvest matcha paired with an artisan's seasonal wagashi sweet. A taste of the tea ceremony, made easy.

items.name: Whisk-Your-Own Matcha
items.desc: Our staff will gently guide you. Whisk your own bowl and enjoy it with a seasonal Japanese sweet (about 40 min).

story.label: Our Story
story.title:
From Uji,
the story of a bowl.
story.body1: Every morning, fresh tea leaves arrive from farmers in Uji, Kyoto. We stone-grind the matcha and whisk it, bowl by bowl, that very same day.
story.body2: It isn't only the quality of the leaves. The water temperature, the warming of the bowl, the motion of the whisk — every small gesture carries our wish for the most delicious bowl possible.

steps.title: Selecting the leaves
steps.desc: Only first-harvest tencha, sourced directly from Uji tea farmers.

steps.title: Stone-grinding
steps.desc: Slowly ground on a stone mill each morning to draw out aroma and umami.

steps.title: Whisking with care
steps.desc: Soft water at 70°C and a bamboo whisk create a fine, smooth foam.

steps.title: Pouring the bowl
steps.desc: Served with care in bowls crafted by Kyoto-ware artisans.

items.text: The gentlest matcha I've ever had. The bowl they whisked by hand had a perfect balance of bitter and umami — close your eyes and you're in a quiet tea room.
items.name: Misaki Tanaka

items.text: I stop by every time I'm in Kyoto. The space is beautiful, and the staff's hospitality is truly special. The matcha parfait was incredible!
items.name: Sarah M.

items.text: The whisk-your-own experience was so much fun. They taught me kindly, and the bowl I made myself was extraordinary. Perfect to recommend to someone special.
items.name: Kenichi Yamamoto

visit.label: Visit Us
visit.title:
Just drop by,
whenever you like.
visit.sub: We don't take reservations — simply come as you are.<br class="pc-only">If we're full, there may be a short wait for a seat.
